pull.title: test: fix intermittent failure in p2p_tx_download.py
pull.body: Because `nodes[1]` time was not mocked in test_block_inv, it was possible for wall clock to advance 2s by the time `nodes[0]` had delivered a tx announcement to it. Then, `nodes[1]` would request the tx from a test peer, never receive the tx, and fail in sync_mempools().

It's possible to simulate `nodes[1]` not running with the following diff on 8130b3b8836879915e82730eb818ee6b58c28168:

```diff
diff --git a/test/functional/p2p_tx_download.py b/test/functional/p2p_tx_download.py
index aa43cc18e2..4a83e44b91 100755
--- a/test/functional/p2p_tx_download.py
+++ b/test/functional/p2p_tx_download.py
@@ -116,6 +116,8 @@ class TxDownloadTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
         self.log.info("Put the tx in node 0's mempool")
         self.nodes[0].sendrawtransaction(tx['hex'])
 
+        time.sleep(2)
+
         # Since node 1 is connected outbound to an honest peer (node 0), it
         # should get the tx within a timeout.
         # However, node 0 sees the same connection as inbound, so it may not
```

I tested the master and PR versions using the same binary and Crypt-iQ's reproducer, adding a delay after `sendrawtransaction`.

On master, with a 2-second delay, 2/5 runs failed due to mempool sync timeouts. With the PR, both runs passed. Increasing the delay to 5 seconds made master pass, but runs took around 83 seconds instead of 26, while the PR remained around 26 seconds.

Looking at node1's debug log, master requests the wtx from peer 4, which never responds, and retries node0 only after 60 seconds. With the PR, it requests from peer 0 almost immediately after receiving the inventory. So this isn't just fixing a flaky test; it also avoids a silent 60-second slowdown when the race occurs.

Concept ACK on splitting this into two subtests. But one thing to watch for in the rework is that `INBOUND_INVENTORY_BROADCAST_INTERVAL` is a mean that is passed to `rand_exp_duration`, and it's not an upper bound. And so bumping node 0 by roughly that interval only covers the draw about 2/3 of the time.

So I tried this and applied this branch locally. I changed node 0's bump from `timeout` to 5 seconds, and then I ran `test_inv_block` 20 times. I got 6 failures, all at the `inv_to_send` assertion. With the existing bump, I got 20 out of 20 passed.

There was #35324, which introduced this assertion with a comment that it may fail rarely and retry the test. So that means that sizing that bump to the interval would turn that rare failure into an actual routine one.

There's a function, `test_tx_requests`, in this file that handles the same problem by bumping in a loop until the expected getdata arrives. That approach I think would work here and would let the caveat be dropped.

> But one thing to watch for in the rework is that INBOUND_INVENTORY_BROADCAST_INTERVAL is a mean that is passed to rand_exp_duration

I think bumping to a reasonable amount over is fine to make the chance of this happening low. Looping also works, though maybe we could just cap the timers in net_processing.cpp

events.message:
test: fix intermittent failure in p2p_tx_download.py

Because nodes[1] time was not mocked in test_inv_block, it was
possible for wall clock to advance 2s by the time nodes[0] had
delivered a tx announcement to it. Then, nodes[1] would request
the tx from a test peer, never receive the tx, and fail in
sync_mempools(). Fix this by using mocktime for nodes[1] as well.

Another issue is that nodes[0] would immediately announce the
tx which usually made nodes[1] request it from them instead
of from a blocking inbound peer. Fix this by ensuring that
nodes[1] requests from a blocking inbound peer first.

events.body: Latest push to 4cc74b2b602d6b64364b91e1e8f9768f78d21b6d uses mocktime and ensures that `self.nodes[1]` requests from a blocking inbound peer first. It is also slightly faster. I will run the patch under `rr` and see if I've introduced any flakes.

> > But one thing to watch for in the rework is that INBOUND_INVENTORY_BROADCAST_INTERVAL is a mean that is passed to rand_exp_duration
> 
> I think bumping to a reasonable amount over is fine to make the chance of this happening low. Looping also works, though maybe we could just cap the timers in net_processing.cpp

Yeap. Agreed. Would also be interested to see whether a cap would apply to some of the other tests on #19732.

Tested on macOS arm64. The PR passed 20/20 runs, and Crypt-iQ's reproducer (2s delay after sendrawtransaction) passed 10/10 runs.

For comparison, my Nov 20 runs on master with the same delay failed 2/5 times due to mempool sync timeouts.

Didn't test on other OSes or with rr though, but looks good from my testing too.

comments.body: you can remove both, the outer loop already takes care of this.

I think if you select `        self.nodes[1].setmocktime(now)` the test will break, because `NONPREF_PEER_TX_DELAY` can never hit? Sure, it never hit in practise before either, but it seems a bit odd for the test to imply it can be hit when now it can deterministically never hit. 

Also, what does "races" refer to when both nodes use mocktime? The patch here doesn't seem right, or at least incomplete.

I think the issue you are seeing was introduced in 2706c5b7c8 (I haven't tried this).

So the possible fixes are:

* Revert 2706c5b7c8 (and go back to rough "best-effort" test coverage)
* Properly use mocktime to keep the test coverage (and ideally exercise the exact code triggers mentioned here)

I should have spent a bit more time before opening the PR. I do think there's a flake here though.

I think currently the test is broken on master:
- `self.nodes[0]` uses mocktime and `self.nodes[1]` does not. So when `self.nodes[0].bumpmocktime(timeout)` is used, it doesn't make much sense because that timeout is actually meant for `self.nodes[1]` since it doesn't have the tx and may request the tx from the test peers and then fallback to requesting it from `self.nodes[0]`. I think `self.nodes[0]` mocktime does need to be bumped, but only around the order of `INBOUND_INVENTORY_BROADCAST_INTERVAL` so it can actually announce to `self.nodes[1]`.
- the second thing is that because `self.nodes[1]` does not use mock time, its real clock can advance before `self.nodes[0]` sends the inv. If time advances on `self.nodes[1]` by `NONPREF_PEER_TX_DELAY` before `self.nodes[0]` can announce, `self.nodes[1]` will request from a test peer first. It will expire after ~60s (`GETDATA_TX_INTERVAL`) and while this is happening, the `sync_mempools` timeout of 60s may be hit.

Is this too much of an edge case?

Sorry, I pasted the wrong commit id :(

I've edited my comment with the correct id. 

I agree that there is a flake here, and it could make sense to fix it. However, I think the correct fix is going to look different.

> Properly use mocktime to keep the test coverage (and ideally exercise the exact code triggers mentioned here)

I think it makes more sense to do this and split into two subtests where one subtest checks behavior when `self.nodes[1]` requests from a non-preferred peer first and the other checks behavior when `self.nodes[1]` requests from `self.nodes[0]` first.
sgtm. Happy to review a pull doing that :)

I'm a little confused what `test_inv_block` is testing. Is it testing that even peers that inv the tx first and never provide it ("block" delivery of the tx) can't prevent the node from getting the tx? Because if so, it seems a little odd because in the real world, `self.nodes[1]` would request the tx from its other peers after ~2s as `self.nodes[0]` would only announce after ~5s. But the test immediately bumps the mocktime of `self.nodes[0]` so it ~instantly announces to `self.nodes[1]` and usually `self.nodes[1]` will request from `self.nodes[0]` instead of from its other peers. This doesn't match reality, so I'm confused.

Yeah, I think this was another bug introduced in 2706c5b7c8eee7ffd8c3b23a8012f346165ddb93? It dropped the NONPREF_PEER_TX_DELAY sleep.

Not sure if there is another test case already for the outbound announcing first, but I think it would be good to write two test cases, or at a minimum fix this test case to add back the `NONPREF_PEER_TX_DELAY` properly.
I did this in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36891/changes/761ec7ee8c3277546cf6375af05b93fd32ae79b4 which also removed another location

I tested that commit and it did introduce the bug. I modified the test to use mocktime and request from a blocking inbound peer first in 4cc74b2b602d6b64364b91e1e8f9768f78d21b6d. I decided against adding a subtest for an outbound announcing first since `test_preferred_tiebreaker_inv` covers this case and, to me, it doesn't really test a peer blocking relay. It mostly seems like an artifact of https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/2706c5b7c8eee7ffd8c3b23a8012f346165ddb93. Also, the whole `p2p_tx_download.py` suite takes ~20s to run on my machine, compared to the commit before https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/2706c5b7c8eee7ffd8c3b23a8012f346165ddb93 which took ~90s to run.
